about: What a working OpenCore config must contain for a given machine. The Windows builder applies these (policy.py) and the Mac app checks an installed EFI against them. Each rule id is the rule name policy.py records for the same change, and tests/test_efi_rules.py proves a policy-built config passes every rule. match = hardware facts, when = config facts that must also hold, expect = what the config must contain; a failed expect is one issue, and fixing it applies exactly the expect. scope: stick = the 1401 installer stick, installed = the EFI an installed Mac boots from.

rules.title: WhateverGreen can crash macOS 26 with your AMD graphics card
rules.what: On macOS 26 Tahoe, WhateverGreen's AMD display patching can panic at startup. Machines with an AMD card and no Intel graphics run without it.
steps: Under Kernel > Add, set Enabled to false on WhateverGreen.kext.
If boot-args has agdpmod=pikera, remove it and add the AGDP board-id patch under Kernel > Patch instead.
rules.source: Dortania Tahoe page

rules.title: Intel Bluetooth needs one boot setting on macOS 26
rules.what: The Intel Bluetooth driver only loads on macOS 26 Tahoe with -ibtcompatbeta in boot-args.
steps: Under NVRAM > Add > 7C436110-AB2A-4BBB-A880-FE41995C9F82, add -ibtcompatbeta to boot-args.
rules.source: Dortania Tahoe page

rules.title: macOS 26 updates can stop at the prohibited sign
rules.what: macOS 26 checks the Mac model during startup and updates. RestrictEvents answers that check when revpatch includes sbvmm.
steps: In boot-args, add revpatch=sbvmm (or add ,sbvmm to an existing revpatch=).
rules.source: the same bypass OCLP applies on unsupported Macs

rules.title: CpuTopologyRebuild freezes desktop Arrow Lake installs
rules.what: With CpuTopologyRebuild loaded, the installer froze right after "PCI configuration end" on Core Ultra 200 desktops. The configuration that installed and runs macOS 15 on a Core Ultra 5 225F does not load it.
steps: Under Kernel > Add, set Enabled to false on CpuTopologyRebuild.kext.
Remove any ctrsmt option from boot-args.
rules.source: a Core Ultra 5 225F that runs macOS 15

rules.match_why: A Mac whose firmware already hands macOS no DMAR table (VT-d off in the BIOS) needs nothing here: the Core Ultra 5 225F that runs macOS 26 has no DMAR in its firmware tables and no ACPI > Delete entry. The Mac app reads the live ACPI tables and sets firmware_no_dmar.
rules.title: Core Ultra PCs freeze before macOS starts with VT-d on
rules.what: Every Core Ultra PC that reached the desktop had VT-d off. Dropping VT-d's table in OpenCore does the same for macOS, and works where the BIOS hides the switch. Windows and Linux keep VT-d.
steps: Under ACPI > Delete, add an entry with TableSignature DMAR, All true, Enabled true.
Or turn VT-d off in the BIOS (sometimes on the overclocking page).
rules.source: 1401 #10, #11 and chat reports, 245KF to 290HX

rules.title: VT-d has to stay out of macOS on Core Ultra
rules.what: DisableIoMapper keeps macOS from using VT-d, which Core Ultra PCs need to start.
steps: Under Kernel > Quirks, set DisableIoMapper to true.

rules.title: 12th-gen and newer Intel laptops stop at EXITBS:START with DevirtualiseMmio on
rules.what: On Intel laptops with performance and efficiency cores, startup can fault before macOS starts with DevirtualiseMmio on. Six of seven public laptop setups that run macOS on these CPUs have it off.
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DevirtualiseMmio to false.
Turn VT-d off in the BIOS; if it still stops at EXITBS:START, turn off Hyper-Threading too.
rules.source: 1401 #6 (13650HX: type 14 fault with it on); public laptop EFIs on 12th to 14th gen and Arrow Lake

rules.title: Core Ultra 200 desktops start with DevirtualiseMmio on
rules.what: A Core Ultra 5 225F desktop runs macOS 26 with DevirtualiseMmio on, and in our reports Arrow Lake desktops reached the installer only with it on (2 of 20 on, 0 of 11 off).
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DevirtualiseMmio to true.
Make sure VT-d is off in the BIOS.
rules.source: a Core Ultra 5 225F that runs macOS 26; 1401 stick reports

rules.scope_why: Installer stick only. The Mac app's setup (nullmoth-setup.sh) adds boot-args to NVRAM Delete on the EFI a Mac starts from, on purpose, so OpenCore rewrites the driver's boot flags every start; of 196 stick configs uploaded 10-20 to 10-25 that delete boot-args, 180 carry 1401's own logging setting and 154 the driver's boot-args, so they are 1401 sticks changed after the build.
rules.title: This EFI can wipe your installed system's boot settings
rules.what: With boot-args under NVRAM > Delete, one start from this EFI replaces the boot flags an installed macOS needs, and it can then refuse to start.
rules.source: a user whose -no_compat_check was wiped by the stick

rules.title: A failed start leaves no log
rules.what: With file logging on, OpenCore saves its log and any macOS panic to the EFI partition, so 1401 can tell you why a start failed instead of you photographing the screen.
steps: Under Misc > Debug, add 65 to Target (logging on, written to a file).
Set AppleDebug and ApplePanic to true.
rules.source: OpenCore Configuration, Misc > Debug

rules.title: The macOS installer is hidden in the boot menu
rules.what: The installer is a recovery entry, which OpenCore hides with HideAuxiliary on. The boot menu then shows only Windows.
steps: Under Misc > Boot, set HideAuxiliary to false.
rules.source: 552 uploaded configs had it on; Dortania installer guide

rules.title: The boot menu never appears
rules.what: Without the boot menu you can't pick the installer, or the Remove NVIDIA driver entry if the driver ever stops your desktop.
steps: Under Misc > Boot, set ShowPicker to true.
rules.source: chat: "remove nvidia driver doesnt exist even when i press space"

rules.title: The boot menu can't show the Remove driver entry
rules.what: Apple's boot menu style lists only systems, never OpenCore tools, so the driver's Remove entry can't appear in it.
steps: Under Misc > Boot, set PickerMode to Builtin (or External).
rules.source: chat: "remove nvidia driver doesnt exist even when i press space"

rules.title: 1401 can't tell which EFI your Mac started from
rules.what: OpenCore shares which partition it started from only when ExposeSensitiveData includes 1. It shares the boot path only, no serial numbers.
steps: Under Misc > Security, add 1 to ExposeSensitiveData (6 becomes 7).
rules.source: the Mac app stopped with one OpenCore partition in sight

rules.title: A file is listed twice in config.plist
rules.what: OpenCore's validator refuses a config that lists the same SSDT or kext twice. The second copy never did anything.
steps: Under ACPI > Add and Kernel > Add, delete the second entry of any file listed twice.
rules.source: ocvalidate

rules.title: USBInjectAll and USBToolBox are both on
rules.what: Both kexts map USB ports, and configs with both on crashed at startup with "element modified after free", sometimes before the NVIDIA driver loaded. USBToolBox with its UTBMap.kext is the one to keep.
steps: Under Kernel > Add, set Enabled to false on USBInjectAll.kext.
rules.source: 21 kernel panics 'element modified after free'; all 11 with a config had this pair or the next one

rules.title: IntelMausi and IntelSnowMausi are both on
rules.what: Both kexts drive the same Intel Ethernet controller, and configs with both on crashed at startup with "element modified after free". Keep one: IntelMausi is the one for current macOS.
steps: Under Kernel > Add, set Enabled to false on IntelSnowMausi.kext.
rules.source: 21 kernel panics 'element modified after free'; all 11 with a config had this pair or the previous one

rules.title: Ryzen startup stops at EB.MM.AKM with SetupVirtualMap on
rules.what: On Ryzen boards newer than the 300 series, boot.efi can't place the kernel in memory with SetupVirtualMap on (EB.MM.AKM, STOP 0x16).
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set SetupVirtualMap to false.
rules.source: stick logs 10-07; Dortania AMD Zen config

rules.title: Ryzen startup stops at EB.MM.AKM with DevirtualiseMmio on
rules.what: Every Ryzen 1000 to 5000 stick that passed boot.efi had DevirtualiseMmio off (1 stop in more than 150 boots).
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DevirtualiseMmio to false.
rules.source: 1401 1.0.14 stick logs; Dortania AMD Zen config

rules.title: Ryzen 7000, 8000 and 9000 stop at EB.MM.AKM without two memory settings
rules.what: On Zen 4 and Zen 5, startup stopped at EB.MM.AKM in 60 boots and passed in 14 with DevirtualiseMmio off. With it and SetupVirtualMap on, boards that had stopped passed on their next start.
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DevirtualiseMmio and SetupVirtualMap to true.
rules.source: every stick log through 2026-10-10; five AM5 boards before and after

rules.title: Ryzen 9000 installs froze about 19 minutes in
rules.what: The installer froze while writing settings to the board's firmware. With DisableVariableWrite on, the install finished. macOS then can't save its own startup disk choice; OpenCore still sets it at every start.
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DisableVariableWrite to true.
rules.source: 1401 issue #30

rules.title: MmioWhitelist entries are on without DevirtualiseMmio
rules.what: Whitelist entries only do something with DevirtualiseMmio on, and OpenCore's validator refuses them without it.
steps: Under Booter > MmioWhitelist, set Enabled to false on every entry.
rules.source: ocvalidate

rules.title: Startup can stop with STOP 0x16 when low memory is full
rules.what: AllowRelocationBlock gives boot.efi a way to load the kernel when no memory slot fits. It's used only then, so machines that already start never touch it.
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set AllowRelocationBlock to true.
rules.source: 14 sticks stopped at EB.MM.AKMr2

rules.title: A kernel patch fails OpenCore's validator
rules.what: Some patch bytes sit outside ReplaceMask, so they're never written and the validator refuses the config. Clearing them changes nothing OpenCore does.
steps: Under Kernel > Patch, make each Replace equal to Replace AND ReplaceMask.
rules.source: ocvalidate

rules.title: macOS can write to your board's firmware in a way that stopped boards from starting
rules.what: With the memory map rewritten, settings macOS saved to firmware stopped several AMD boards from powering on, some needing a BIOS flashback. DisableVariableWrite blocks those writes.
steps: Under Booter > Quirks, set DisableVariableWrite to true.

rules.title: macOS 26 stops at the Apple logo with your Realtek Ethernet setup
rules.what: macOS 26 adds its own Realtek driver, which needs a system part your Wi-Fi setup blocks. Lucy already drives the port, so Apple's driver is blocked too.
steps: Under Kernel > Block, add com.apple.driver.AppleEthernetRL with Strategy Exclude, MinKernel 25.0.0, Enabled true.
rules.source: Tahoe with the IOSkywalkFamily downgrade

rules.title: Your NVMe drive can drop out under macOS
rules.what: This drive model can disappear under macOS power management. NVMeFix clears that on the drive families it's known to help.
steps: Under Kernel > Add, set Enabled to true on NVMeFix.kext.
rules.source: storage_drives.py

builder_only.about: policy.py changes that are build decisions, not facts a working EFI must match. The Mac checker never reports these.
